subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song suggested bypassing swap readahead for zswap, but noted that a better readahead policy is needed to avoid increased unmapping costs. They proposed evaluating shadow as a stronger hint for readahead and implementing proactive aging or a similar approach.
reviews.raw_body:
That's a really nice POC! We should do that IMO, maybe with better
support for (m)THP readahead too.

We first need a better readahead policy though, or else unmapping
these folios might cost even more.

For the readahead part I'm thinking about evaluating using shadow as a
stronger hint for readahead after MGLRU-FG which helps distribute the
folios based on frequencey more evenly among gens, also with a more
proactive aging (async aging, or maybe lru_gen_imbalanced as Barry
once suggested somewhere) so folios in the same gen with same freq
will be much more likely to be reused. Or something similiar to file
readahead's PG_readahead based readahead. Well more
experiments are needed first though.

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch bypasses swap readahead for zswap, an in-memory synchronous backend similar to zram. The current implementation of swap readahead can lead to pointless prefetching of pages, causing increased anon residency and page cache thrashing. By bypassing readahead for zswap, the patch aims to reduce this overhead and improve performance. Measurements show significant gains in build time, zswap-in/out rates, and reduced swap readahead hits. The patch reuses existing code and adds a new helper function to check if a swap entry is synchronous.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: reviewer asked about potential regressions with the zswap shrinker enabled and both zswap and disk swap backends present
reviews.raw_body:
Would there be regression with shrinker on, when we have mixed zswap
and disk swap backends?
